name: What is the difference between open-cell and closed-cell spray foam insulation for walls?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between open-cell and closed-cell spray foam insulation for walls?

acceptedAnswer.text: Open-cell and closed-cell spray foam are two distinct types of insulation. Open-cell foam is softer and more flexible, with a lower R-value per inch, and primarily functions as an air barrier. It's often more affordable and can allow moisture to pass through. Closed-cell foam is denser, more rigid, and has a higher R-value per inch, acting as both an air and vapor barrier. It also adds structural integrity to walls. The choice depends on specific needs for R-value, moisture control, and structural support.
acceptedAnswer.description: Open-cell foam is softer, lower R-value, and an air barrier. Closed-cell foam is denser, higher R-value, and acts as an air and vapor barrier, offering structural support.
